From the screenshots, the browser is telling you a stylesheet referenced in your HTML (at (index):8) couldn’t be fetched/applied. The snippet 500;600&display=swap is a dead giveaway that the “stylesheet” is probably a Google Fonts CSS URL (e.g., fonts.googleapis.com/css2?...wght@400;500;600&display=swap).

That usually doesn’t break a site completely by itself (you’d just get fallback fonts), so when a Vercel page “doesn’t load,” it’s often because one or more critical CDN resources are blocked or returning the wrong thing, and this is just the first visible symptom.

Most common causes

Network / firewall / DNS blocking Google Fonts or Tailwind CDN

Corporate networks and some campus networks often block fonts.googleapis.com, fonts.gstatic.com, or CDN endpoints.

Privacy tools can also block them.

An extension is blocking it (adblock/privacy/tracker protection)

uBlock / Brave Shields / “privacy badger” style extensions commonly block Google Fonts and some CDNs.

This produces exactly this kind of “failed to load stylesheet” signal.

The URL returns HTML (or a redirect) instead of CSS

Example: the request gets rewritten to your app’s index.html, a login page, a consent page, or a 404 HTML page.

Browsers will refuse to apply it as a stylesheet if the Content-Type is wrong (or if strict MIME checking kicks in).

CSP (Content Security Policy) blocks it

If the site sets Content-Security-Policy and doesn’t allow that domain in style-src, the stylesheet load will be refused.

In that case you’d usually also see a console message explicitly mentioning CSP.
